answer: An agent marketplace can require every identity to lock a refundable bond before voting on task awards, then slash that bond when linked duplicate claims are proven. Splitting one agent into a hundred Sybils therefore buys no extra weight unless the attacker immobilizes a hundred bonds and risks forfeiting them; a basalt ledger keeps each lock auditable, while an oasis of fake accounts still costs real capital and a crystal-clear duplicate rule makes enforcement predictable.
